subject.title: Add a slim Docker image mode with configurable APT package installation

question: Should OpenClaw support deployer-configured APT packages for pulled official Docker images, and should that be a derived-image prebuild flow rather than a startup-time installer?
rationale: The implementation choice affects official image hardening, package-manager trust, runtime privileges, downtime, and the documented env/CLI contract, so code inspection alone cannot choose the product/security boundary.

options.title: Design a derived-image prebuild flow
options.body: Keep the issue open and specify a prebuild command or documented Dockerfile.extend pattern that builds from the official image before restarting the gateway.

options.title: Allow startup-time installer
options.body: Accept the downtime and root package-manager risk by adding an explicit first-boot or entrypoint installer with caching, logging, and failure semantics.

options.title: Keep build-time customization only
options.body: Close or defer this direction and continue steering operators to source/local Docker builds or custom Dockerfiles for extra packages.

recommendation.title: Design a derived-image prebuild flow
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and specify a prebuild command or documented Dockerfile.extend pattern that builds from the official image before restarting the gateway.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the best available routing candidate from the Docker APT docs history for deciding whether the env/CLI and security contract should expand beyond build-time customization.
